source_text: Huius itaque appetitus non in genere suo, non in specie, non in modo culpa est, sed in excessu: quia genus eius et species ad conditoris operam pertinent, modus eius ad arbitrium honestatis, excessus ad vitium voluntatis Post longam disputationem velut concludens: "Merito igitur concupiscentiae origo definitur in igne vitali, quo collecto necesse est ut ei reputetur concupiscentia carnalis, per quem constitit vita carnalis
pass_a_gloss: Of-this and-so appetite not in genere his-own, not in specie, not in now/only fault is, but in excessu: because genus his/its and species to founder operam pertinent, modus his/its to decision decency, excessus to vice of-will after longam disputationem as-if concludens: " deservedly therefore of-desire origin is-defined in igne vitali, whither collecto necessary is so-that/as to-him reputetur desire carnal, through whom constitit life carnal.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS conditor; Blaise God as maker from nothing

pass_b_english: Sexual desire’s origin is therefore rightly defined as lying in the fire of life. Once this has been established, bodily desire must be attributed to the one through whom bodily life came into being.

So this appetite is not blameworthy in its general kind, its particular form, or its proper measure, but in its excess. Its kind and form belong to the Creator’s work; its measure to the choice of honorable conduct; its excess to the fault of the will.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
